expectations.evidence: 3 distinct proposals: 方案一(物品池固有特性), 方案二(温度系统), 方案三(池子阵型).

expectations.text: Each proposal has all required sections (想法/规则变更/分析)
expectations.evidence: Each has an intro paragraph (≈想法), 具体规则变更/具体规则(≈规则变更), and 为什么这样设计/策略影响/优势(≈分析). Content equivalent.

expectations.text: Rule changes specify actual modifications to pool mechanics
expectations.evidence: 方案一: 5 specific pool traits with exact numbers (25% extra item, quality shift formula, cross-rarity merging, 2x recycle value, polarized probability distribution). 方案二: temperature 0-100, +15/-5 per draw, threshold effects at 30/70. 方案三: 5 named formations with specific affix combinations.

expectations.text: Proposals reference actual pool mechanics accurately
expectations.evidence: References 5 item pools by name, 7 affixes by Chinese name, current refresh mechanics, rarity weights, merging rules. All accurate.
方案三 is explicitly 'most minimal change' (just changes refresh rules). 方案一 adds 5 new trait mechanics. 方案二 introduces dynamic state. Recommendation section suggests implementing in order of ambition.

expectations.text: Each proposal explains HOW it creates stronger differentiation and meaningful choice
expectations.evidence: 方案一: trait+affix combos create strategic depth (with 3 concrete examples). 方案二: temperature creates dynamic trade-off between cost and quality. 方案三: formations make pools relate to each other as a 'situation' not independent options.

expectations.text: Proposals describe mechanics in ordinary language
expectations.evidence: Trait names (丰产/精炼/标准化/回锅/高压) are plain descriptive Chinese words for the mechanical effects. '温度' and '阵型' are standard metaphors. No invented compound jargon.

expectations.text: Added complexity is justified as necessary for differentiation
expectations.evidence: 方案三 exists as minimal option. Recommendation explicitly suggests layered approach: 'start with 方案三 to validate, then add 方案一 if pool category still feels same'. Complexity is staged and justified by what each layer solves.

expectations.text: Analysis addresses whether pool differentiation risks reducing fun of the current draw experience
expectations.evidence: No explicit fun-risk discussion. Doesn't address: could traits make some pools feel bad? Could temperature make 'cold' pools frustrating? Could formations reduce the surprise of random affix combinations?

eval_feedback.overall: Consistently strong output. The fun_impact assertion is the same blind spot as all without-skill runs.
